title: Anthropic or open ai should acquire a game studio
author: HamsterUnfair6313
selftext:
Currently they're scraping github and tutorials online. Training on quality codebase from a legit game studio will accelerate quality games

It would great if they acquire rockstar studios or EA or ubisoft etc

To make AA or AAA games in a weekend

comments.author: Kanzes
comments.body: with what lol they're burning money

comments.author: wahoozerman
comments.body: If this logic were particularly sound, you'd think copilot would be good at it. But it sure isn't.

replies.author: HamsterUnfair6313
replies.body: I don't think they used Xbox games for training copilot

comments.author: twendah
comments.body: lol no, those repos are full of spaghetti code dude

comments.author: Valdaraak
comments.body:
If I'm paying $70+ for a AAA game, I don't want it flooded with AI. If $70 AAA games go that route, I'll start just making my own or sticking with indie games.

And there are very real limitations that you run into when you work on a project the size of a AAA game fully with AI. Large codebases like that are so massive and interconnected that an agent will run out of context before it manages to fully trace for the thing you're asking it to do.

replies.author: HamsterUnfair6313
replies.body:
Chatgpt and Claude scraped entire internet. I don't think you have to worry about couple of games code base. 

They will quantize the model and train its weights

replies.author: Valdaraak
replies.body: I don't think you full understand how agents work with existing code bases.

replies.author: HamsterUnfair6313
replies.body: A shitty game like wolverine costed them 30 million dollars lol. With ai cost could have been cut

replies.author: Novaworld7
replies.body: You are already getting AI in your 70+ dollar game.

replies.author: Valdaraak
replies.body: I am aware of that. I said "flooded". I didn't say no AI at all.

replies.author: Both_Lawfulness6708
replies.body: Does AI make the games worse?

replies.author: Ok-Pirate5732
replies.body: It's effectiveness certainly drops off the more complex it is lol

comments.author: streetwearvc
comments.body: why? lol you know video games have spaghetti code. its assets that are the main value

replies.author: HamsterUnfair6313
replies.body: In game physics, camera movement, consistency and flow of logic and consequences of actions. Story and dialogues

replies.author: streetwearvc
replies.body:
yeah this is a dumb take. massively bad code goes into games because video gamers are notorious for being bad at design choices. 

ex: polygon count for renders (cyberpunk releases) — too much detail or water or trees where the game lags because of it. 

There’s so many things that you need to be aware of that has trade offs for video games. If you knew game design - you would understand this.

replies.author: HamsterUnfair6313
replies.body: Poor optimization exists i agree, but it can be evaluated by human devs and adjusted

replies.author: streetwearvc
replies.body: trust me i work in inference and i train my own models. training in video games would be the worst option because the reward system is inherently bad for gaming when it comes to coding.

comments.author: Im_Action
comments.body: games are not successful being openly ai coded

comments.author: Fruitsy
comments.body: the IP's and characters are more important than any code

comments.author: dorcsyful
comments.body:
Have you seen how much at a loss they are operating at? Even if they weren't, their codebase is miniscule compared to what they are getting from "free" resources.
Also think about this: the average AAA game starts at 40. If a new game gets released every week (impossible) people will simply either not buy them because they barely played the one released last week our they'll simply have no money to buy all of them. That's a very fast way to run a studio to the ground

replies.author: HamsterUnfair6313
replies.body: Isn't that the end goal of AI. To automate all jobs and devalue human labor? Produce acceptable slop at cheaper costs.

replies.author: dorcsyful
replies.body: I mean that's their end goal yes. Whether or not that's good for humanity is highly debatable. Again, if human labor has no value humans won't have money. And then we're back to a bunch of slop games being released and no one has money to buy them

comments.author: zenmatrix83
comments.body: there are tons of open engines on the internet and both are vaccuming up all code from github, research papers, and anything else. both are more concerned with showing how good the ai is and solving centries old math and other problems, gaming is not a real concern for them

comments.author: ForgePointGames
comments.body: Solo dev here, I shipped one game with AI help and my second launches this month. The bottleneck was never the code. It was knowing what's fun. A AAA game made in a weekend would just have a weekend's worth of design decisions.

comments.author: daddywookie
comments.body: I can’t imagine a worse tutor than an actual codebase from a long running game project. And don’t even think of trying to use the studio team structure or business practices either. I swear it is a miracle if any large game gets released.

comments.author: siberianmi
comments.body: I don’t think that the models need a lot of acceleration what they need at this point it’s just people driving them who know what they’re doing. I mean a few point one of the frontier models at a code base that’s having a frame rate problem and tell it to optimize it and leave it alone. It’ll come back and tell you exactly where the problem was and find you a bunch of ways to pick up extra frames per second.  It’s already more than good enough with code. More training code base on game development specifically is really not going to help it.

comments.author: Neither-Upstairs
comments.body: This is such a bad take
